STATUS: fail

SUMMARY: Three reproduced failures: a HEAD response with no body and no Content-Length carries the tag of the empty body, `Flush` sends bytes before the handler finishes (which contradicts the approved-difference line), and `Compress(ETag(h))` gives gzip and identity responses the same strong ETag. The listed criteria and the other hostile inputs I probed held. The probe file is deleted and `git status` matches the start.

FILES TOUCHED: middleware/zz_redteam_probe_test.go (created and deleted; no other files changed)

FINDINGS:
- [blocking] HEAD with no body and no Content-Length gets a computed ETag of the empty body. `HEAD ETag "e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb924"` vs GET `"2cf24dba5fb0a30e26e83b2ac5b9e29e"` for a handler that writes "hello" only on GET. This is the triggered check ("a HEAD response never carries a validator computed from an empty body"). Fix in `finish`: skip the computed tag when the request is HEAD and the buffer is empty.
- [blocking] Flush sends bytes early. Real server, handler writes "part1", flushes, then blocks: "part1" reaches the client before the handler completes. The APPROVED DIFFERENCES line says Flush must not send bytes before completion, but criterion 9 requires Flush to commit and flush. These cannot both hold. Not resolved by the code; see OPEN QUESTIONS.
- [blocking] `ETag(Compress(5,"text/plain")(h))` gives gzip and identity different ETags, but `Compress(5,…)(ETag(h))` gives the same strong ETag `"71a0f557…"` for gzip (Content-Encoding gzip) and identity. A strong validator shared across content-codings violates RFC 9110 §8.8.1. Reproduced with `go test -race -run TestRTProbeCompressOrder`.
- [minor] GET handler that sets Content-Length 5 and writes nothing gets no ETag (criterion 2 says an empty GET body still gets one). Reproduced; this is a self-inconsistent handler, so low severity.
- [minor] `If-None-Match: *, "a"` matches `"a"`. The `*` is treated as junk and `"a"` matches. RFC allows `*` only alone, so this is lenient, not a crash. Not a finding for the criteria.

CHECKS:
- `TestRTProbeHeadEmptyBodyTag` (HEAD vs GET, handler writes only on GET) -> FAIL (blocking above)
- `TestRTProbeGetDeclaredLengthNoBody` -> FAIL (minor above)
- `TestRTProbeFlushSendsEarly` (real server, read before release) -> FAIL (blocking above)
- `TestRTProbeResponseController` (SetWriteDeadline + Flush via NewResponseController, real server) -> pass
- `TestRTProbeCompressOrder` (both orders, gzip vs identity, body decodes) -> FAIL for Compress(ETag(h)) (blocking above); ETag(Compress(h)) differs correctly
- `TestRTProbeServeContent` (handler ETag + If-None-Match -> 304 once; no-handler-ETag 200; Range -> 206 "he") -> pass
- `TestRTProbePanicUnderRecoverer` (write then panic under Recoverer) -> pass, 500 with empty body
- `TestRTProbeInformationalOrder` (1xx, then 201 after a body write) -> the first Write fixed 200, which is correct; my expectation was wrong, not a bug
- `TestRTProbeChunkingProperty` (2000 seeded random bodies with random chunking; ETag equals single-write ETag; self If-None-Match gives 304) -> pass
- `TestRTProbeConcurrent` (50 parallel requests, -race) -> pass
- `TestRTProbeHeadNon200` (HEAD 404 with If-None-Match on handler ETag) -> pass
- `TestRTProbeMatchEdges` (obs-text tag matches; control char rejected; `""` matches `""`; `"a,"b"` no match; `"x",,` matches) -> pass, apart from the `*, "a"` leniency noted above
- Existing `Hijack`/`Push` unsupported and forwarded paths, and `Unwrap` identity: read the assertions, which check the real wrapper and the same error strings as compress.go; not re-run as probes

OPEN QUESTIONS:
- Flush contract conflicts: criterion 9 requires Flush to commit and flush the underlying writer, while the APPROVED DIFFERENCES line says Flush must not send bytes before the response completes. The code follows criterion 9, so the approved-difference line does not hold. The orchestrator needs to decide which one is right and fix the other.
- Strong-ETag sharing across Compress(ETag(h)): decide whether this order is supported or documented. If it stays, the README/doc comment should say so.
